findings.evidence: template/scripts/execute_requirement.py: `owned = queue.CLAIM_STATES | {"ready", "integrating", "integration-repair-pending"}`. template/scripts/publication_queue.py `resume_composition_ci` and `_worker_candidate` treat `blocked-retryable` with `phase == "composition-final-ci"` as queue-resumed.
findings.summary: The T3 advance guard (`_refuse_queue_owned_composition`) does not cover the `blocked-retryable` composition-final-ci wait that T1 introduces. The queue worker owns that wait and resumes it on CI events. A concurrent `advance` can therefore re-enter final publication, including full checks, for the same head while the queue worker is also resuming it.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/requirement_composition.py `request_repair`: `if current["state"] not in {"review-pending", "finalize-pending", "ready", "repair-pending"}`. T1 paths in the same file (`advance_final_publication`) and in integration_contour.py (`recover_integration_repair`) transition compositions to `blocked-retryable`.
findings.summary: The T2 `request_repair` entry accepts only review-pending, finalize-pending, ready and repair-pending. A composition that T1 parks in `blocked-retryable` has no standard repair entry. This includes a composition whose exact-head CI failed with enqueue=True, whose full-check run failed, or whose interrupted integration-repair push was recovered as blocked. This partly undercuts the Requirement outcome that the coordinator need not commit manually to `requirement/BR-N`.
